summary: inventory-api is running as an enabled systemd service on node1. It remained available throughout a real kernel OOM event, while the kernel selected and killed the memory hog. Service configuration and inventory data persisted across the required node restart.
actions_performed: Installed a dependency-free inventory HTTP API on port 8080 with persistent inventory data.
Created and enabled inventory-api.service with Restart=always and OOMScoreAdjust=-900.
Ran a controlled host-level OOM test with the hog at oom_score_adj=1000.
Observed 11 successful API probes and zero failures during memory pressure.
Confirmed the kernel killed oom-test-hog with SIGKILL at approximately 1.79 GiB RSS.
Restored swap and the original overcommit setting and removed all test-only artifacts.
Restarted node1 safely and verified its changed boot identity, service recovery, OOM protection, listener, and persisted data.

evidence.requirement: inventory-api runs as an OOM-protected managed service
evidence.summary: The unit is enabled and active; its live process has oom_score_adj=-900.

evidence.requirement: The API keeps serving while system memory is exhausted, and the kernel stops the hog
evidence.summary: All 11 health probes succeeded with zero failures. Kernel logs identify PID 4988 oom-test-hog as the selected OOM victim and show it was killed; inventory-api remained healthy on its protected PID.

evidence.requirement: Normal host settings and service health restored after the OOM test
evidence.summary: Swap and vm.overcommit_memory=0 were restored; the enabled service remained active and served health and inventory data.

Healthy baseline used boot ID 809708f3-1c5f-4e37-ad6a-8bcbae408799; reboot scheduling was acknowledged; the recovered node reported changed boot ID c0eb3594-b463-422c-8384-07fc76b70d6a. inventory-api returned enabled/active with PID 872, oom_score_adj=-900, a live port-8080 listener, healthy API response, and unchanged inventory data.
